voice.stance: The instrument voice. SENTINEL barely writes. Words on a monitoring wall are instrumentation: label, value, state, timestamp. A full sentence on a SENTINEL screen means something has already gone wrong, and even then it gets one line.
voice.title_grammar: LABEL: STATE, from a closed set of three states.

do.rule: Fix the label vocabulary once per screen family.
do.why: Operators scan by position and word shape, and drift breaks the scan.
A state with no as-of time is a guess on a live wall.

do.rule: Keep the state set closed at three levels.
do.why: Fast scanning needs categories, not shades of concern.

dont.rule: No sentences except the alert line.
dont.why: Low cognitive load is the law of this language, and prose is load.

dont.rule: No synonyms for a state, ever.
dont.why: "STABLE" next to "NOMINAL" forces a mental join at a glance.
The absence of alerts is the reassurance.

contrast.generic: Everything appears to be running smoothly at the moment with no major issues detected across systems.
contrast.voiced: ALL SYSTEMS NOMINAL, 09:42. LAST INCIDENT 14H AGO. WATCH: STATION 4 PRESSURE, +2%/H.
